lines.say: Ten best days missed. Fifty-six percent less money.

lines.text: J.P. Morgan tracked $10,000 in the S&P 500 (dividends reinvested), 2006 to 2025. Left alone: $80,619.
lines.say: J.P. Morgan tracked ten thousand dollars in the S and P five hundred, with dividends reinvested, from two thousand six through twenty twenty-five. Left alone, it grew to eighty thousand, six hundred nineteen dollars.

lines.text: Miss only the 10 best days and it's $35,866.
lines.say: Miss only the ten best days, and it's thirty-five thousand, eight hundred sixty-six dollars.

lines.text: That's 10 days out of about 5,000 trading days: 0.2%.
lines.say: That's ten days out of about five thousand trading days. Zero point two percent.

lines.text: Why not just skip the bad days? Squirrel tried. Squirrel can't tell them apart.
lines.say: Why not just skip the bad days? Squirrel tried. Squirrel can't tell them apart.
On March twelfth, twenty twenty, the S and P five hundred fell nine point five percent.
The next day, it jumped nine point three percent.

lines.text: Not a fluke: 6 of the 10 best days came within 2 weeks of the 10 worst.
lines.say: It's not a fluke. Six of the ten best days in those years came within two weeks of the ten worst.

post.title: Missing the 10 Best Days in 20 Years Left 56% Less
post.ig:
Miss the 10 best days in 20 years, end with 56% less.
$10,000 in the S&P 500 (dividends reinvested) from 2006 to 2025 grew to $80,619 left alone (11.0% a year).
Missing only the 10 best days: $35,866 (6.6% a year).
6 of the 10 best days came within 2 weeks of the 10 worst. March 12, 2020: -9.5%. March 13: +9.3%.
Sources: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Guide to Retirement 2026; S&P 500 daily closes, March 2020.
